title: JSON+: Add wildcardfield, protocol-scoped lookups, with per-protocol filters
description:
Add <wildcardfield> XML element to the JSON+ dictionary, allowing object
keys that are values (e.g. DNN names like "web.operator.com", "voice.operator.com" match to alias of json.dnn)
to be matched by regex and dissected using an alias path. Wildcard
children support nested <field>, <array-element>, and <wildcardfield>
elements recursively.

Fix per-packet stale state by resetting jsonplus_dict_active at the top
of dissect_json() each call.

Scope field lookups to the matched protocol: each json_protocol_t now
carries its own wmem_tree_t *fields populated from the fields defined in
the same XML file. jsonplus_lookup_field_by_path() searches the matched
protocol's tree instead of the global dict->fields, preventing fields
from one protocol's XML file applying to packets matched by a different
protocol. Falls back to global dict->fields when no protocols are
defined, if built.

Register a hidden FT_BOOLEAN field per <protocol> element with abbrev
json.<sanitized-name> (e.g. json.nudm_sdm) so matched packets are
filterable by protocol name.

AI-Assisted: yes

+### Wildcard Object Keys (<wildcardfield>)
+
+Some JSON APIs use object keys that are runtime values — DNN names,
+subscription IDs, UUIDs — rather than fixed schema names. A
+`<wildcardfield>` element matches those keys by regex and dissects their
+children using a fixed alias path, so child fields are filterable even
+though the parent key is unknown at schema time.
+
+Syntax:
+<field name="DnnConfigurations" path="dnnConfigurations" type="Object">
+    <wildcardfield name="Apn" path="dnnConfigurations.apn"
+                   displayvalue="name" match=".*\.com">
+        <field name="DefaultSessionType"
+               path="dnnConfigurations.apn.pduSessionTypes.defaultSessionType"
+               type="String"/>
+        <field name="5qi" path="dnnConfigurations.apn.5gQosProfile.5qi"
+               type="Integer"/>
+        <!-- Nested wildcardfield is allowed -->
+        <wildcardfield name="Slice" path="dnnConfigurations.apn.slice"
+                       displayvalue="id" match="[0-9]+">
+            <field name="Sst" path="dnnConfigurations.apn.slice.sst"
+                   type="Integer"/>
+        </wildcardfield>
+    </wildcardfield>
+    <!-- Catch-all after more specific patterns -->
+    <wildcardfield name="AnyKey" path="dnnConfigurations.key"
+                   displayvalue="key" match=".*">
+    </wildcardfield>
+</field>
+
+Attributes:
+- name:         Display name for the wildcard subtree
+- path:         Full path string. The last segment (after the final dot)
+                is the alias token — it replaces the runtime key in all
+                child path lookups. Example: path="dnnConfigurations.apn"
+                → alias "apn", child paths use "dnnConfigurations.apn.*"
+- displayvalue: Label for the auto-generated string field that shows the
+                actual runtime key value. Default: "key".
+                Filter: json.<path>.<displayvalue> == "web.operator.com"
+- match:        PCRE2 regex matched against the runtime JSON key. Required.
+                First matching wildcardfield wins (document order).
+
+Matching priority for each key encountered under the parent object:
+  1. Exact literal <field> lookup by full path — wins if found
+  2. <wildcardfield> entries tried in document order — first match wins
+  3. No match — key displayed as generic JSON
+
+Child elements inside <wildcardfield>:
+  - <field>         — regular child field (path uses alias, not runtime key)
+  - <array-element> — if the wildcard value is an array
+  - <wildcardfield> — nested wildcard (recursive)
+
+Auto-generated key-value field:
+Each <wildcardfield> registers a FT_STRING field at
+json.<path>.<displayvalue> (e.g. json.dnnConfigurations.apn.name).
+This field holds the actual runtime key and is always filterable.
+
+Examples:
+  Filter the key:       json.dnnConfigurations.apn.name == "web.operator.com"
+  Filter a child:       json.dnnConfigurations.apn.5gQosProfile.5qi == 9
+  Filter array child:   json.dnnConfigurations.apn.sscModes.allowedSscModes == "SSC_MODE_1"
+
 ## Integer Enum Mapping
 
 For integer fields, you can define human-readable enum names that map to numeric codes.

+## Wildcard Object Keys
+
+Some JSON objects use runtime values as keys (e.g. DNN names, subscription
+IDs). Use `<wildcardfield>` to match these by regex and dissect their children
+with fixed alias paths:
+
+<field name="DnnConfigurations" path="dnnConfigurations" type="Object">
+    <wildcardfield name="Apn" path="dnnConfigurations.apn"
+                   displayvalue="name" match=".*">
+        <field name="DefaultSessionType"
+               path="dnnConfigurations.apn.pduSessionTypes.defaultSessionType"
+               type="String"/>
+    </wildcardfield>
+</field>
+
+- `path=` — full path; the last segment (`apn`) becomes the alias token
+  substituted for the runtime key in all child path lookups
+- `displayvalue=` — label for the auto-generated string field that shows
+  the actual key value (default: "key")
+- `match=` — PCRE2 regex matched against the runtime JSON key (required)
+
+Matching priority per key: literal `<field>` lookup first, then
+`<wildcardfield>` entries in document order, then generic display.
+
+Filter the key value: `json.dnnConfigurations.apn.name == "web.operator.com"`
+Filter a child field: `json.dnnConfigurations.apn.pduSessionTypes.defaultSessionType == "TYPE"`
+
+See DICTIONARY-GUIDE.txt for full `<wildcardfield>` reference.
+
+## Per-Protocol Field Scoping
+
+When `<protocol>` entries are defined, each protocol's dictionary fields are
+scoped to packets that matched that protocol. Fields from one XML file do not
+apply to packets matched by a protocol defined in a different XML file. This
+prevents cross-contamination between dictionaries.
+
+Fields in XML files with no `<protocol>` element are global and only apply
+when no protocols are defined at all (legacy mode).
+
+## Filtering by Protocol Name
+
+Every `<protocol>` element automatically registers a hidden boolean field:
+
+    json.<sanitized-name>
+
+where the name is lowercased and non-alphanumeric characters replaced with
+underscores. Examples:
+- `<protocol name="NUDM_SDM" ...>` → filter: `json.nudm_sdm`
+- `<protocol name="GitHub API" ...>` → filter: `json.github_api`
+- `<protocol name="5GC Core" ...>` → filter: `json._5gc_core`
+
+Use it to isolate packets matched by that protocol:
+    json.nudm_sdm          (show only NUDM_SDM packets)
+
+The field is registered at startup regardless of whether any packets match,
+so it is always available as a valid filter name.
+
